source_doc_path: .\data\QFaaS _ A serverless Function-as-a-Service Framework for Quantum Computing.pdf

general.purpose: QFaaS is a proposed Quantum Function-as-a-Service framework intended to ease challenges from diverse quantum programming languages and hardware platforms by applying a serverless model and software engineering approaches to practical quantum computing. It is designed to simplify hybrid quantum-classical software development and support the quantum software transition.

type_evidence.evidence: Compose Quantum functions using local IDE or the web-based IDE of QFaaS Dashboard.
A corresponding quantum circuit will be built and then sent to the selected quantum backend according to user input.
Then, that circuit will be transpiled to corresponding quantum system-level languages (such as QASM [9]) before being sent to a quantum cloud service for execution.
End-users can get the result data, and information about the backend device is used for the quantum execution.
Fig. 13. Scalability evaluation on Qiskit QRNG function.
If any issues are discovered during the deployment or invocation, QFaaS will check and provide detailed logs for the engineer to investigate and figure out the problem.

automation_level.evidence: Suppose the end-user does not specify a specific quantum backend, QFaaS could automatically choose the best suitable (least busy) backend at the quantum provider to send the quantum circuit for execution.

evaluation_type.evidence: We present two practical use cases and perform the evaluations on quantum computers and simulators to demonstrate our framework's ability to ease the burden on traditional engineers to expedite the ongoing quantum software transition.

architecture.design_principles: Serverless quantum computing; hybrid quantum-classical functions; unified support for multiple quantum SDKs and languages; multi-provider execution to avoid vendor lock-in; modular architecture; containerized functions; DevOps/CI/CD-based automation; Kubernetes-based orchestration and autoscaling.
architecture.technological_foundation: Kubernetes; Qiskit; Cirq; Q#; Braket; Qiskit Terra API; DevOps; Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD); container-based quantum software environment setup.

orchestrator.evidence: We employed Kubernetes to orchestrate all the pods (the container-based unit of Kubernetes) for the QFaaS function across all cluster nodes.

manager_controller.evidence: QFaaS Automation implements the Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) process, following the DevOps paradigm to ensure the continuous delivery of reliable quantum functions for end-users.

vendor_agnostic_layer.evidence: We design QFaaS as a unified quantum computing framework by supporting well-known quantum languages and software development kits (Qiskit, Q#, Cirq, and Braket), executing the quantum tasks on multiple simulators and quantum cloud providers (IBM Quantum and Amazon Braket).

backend_integration.evidence: Monitor (Physical devices) (External) IBM Quantum, Amazon Braket Fig. 2.

debugging_testing.evidence: If any issues are discovered during the deployment or invocation, QFaaS will check and provide detailed logs for the engineer to investigate and figure out the problem.

simulation_support.evidence: All quantum SDKs and languages have their built-in quantum simulator, which can run directly inside a pod at the Kubernetes cluster.

security_mechanisms.evidence: We will enhance the security and scalability capabilities in QFaaS to support a large number of requests from multiple users.

scalability_mechanisms.evidence: QFaaS also leverages the advantages of Kubernetes to support auto-scaling features, i.e., automatically scaling up or down vertically to adapt to the number of user requests.

telemetry_monitoring.evidence: The Monitoring layer periodically checks the status of the deployment process, function usage, and system status (such as network status, Kubernetes cluster resource consumption) to provide insights for quantum software engineers on demand.

user_interface.evidence: Our framework also provides multiple ways for users to interact with the core components, including QFaaS Dashboard (a modern web-based application), QFaaS CLI (an interactive command-line tool), and QFaaS Core APIs.

algorithms.overall_evidence: We present two practical use cases and perform the evaluations on quantum computers and simulators to demonstrate our framework's ability to ease the burden on traditional engineers to expedite the ongoing quantum software transition.

challenges.statement: QFaaS currently has limited provider access/connectivity and only demonstrates experiments with IBM Quantum and Amazon Braket, with broader provider support left for future work.
challenges.category_evidence: Due to the current limitation around access to quantum cloud services from our region, we are able to demonstrate the experiments with IBM Quantum and Amazon Braket at the moment.
challenges.strength_evidence: We plan to extend QFaaS's ability to connect with other providers in the future.

challenges.statement: The framework's security and scalability capabilities are not yet fully realized and still need enhancement for multi-user demand.
challenges.category_evidence: We will enhance the security and scalability capabilities in QFaaS to support a large number of requests from multiple users.
challenges.strength_evidence: We will enhance the security and scalability capabilities in QFaaS to support a large number of requests from multiple users.

challenges.statement: The authors indicate QFaaS still requires significant research effort to become reliable and keep pace with rapid hardware advances.
challenges.category_evidence: there is a need for significant research effort to make it reliable and simultaneously adapt to rapid advances in quantum hardware.
